question.prompt: Rhombus \(ABCD,\) with side length \(6,\) is rolled to form a cylinder of volume \(6\) by taping \(\overline{AB}\) to \(\overline{DC}.\) What is \(\sin(\angle ABC)?\)

solutions.explanation:
Use the usual interpretation that the rhombus is rolled once without stretching. When \(AB\) is taped to \(DC\), the sides \(AD\) and \(BC\) close into the circular rims. Each has length \(6\), so the cylinder radius \(r\) satisfies
\[
2\pi r=6,\qquad r=\frac{3}{\pi}.
\]
The cylinder height \(h\) is the perpendicular distance between \(AD\) and \(BC\) in the flat rhombus. Write \(\theta=\angle ABC\). Dropping an altitude gives
\[
h=6\sin\theta.
\]
This remains true if \(\theta\) is obtuse, because its supplementary acute angle has the same sine.

Now apply the cylinder volume formula:
\[
6=\pi r^2h
=\pi\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)^2(6\sin\theta)
=\frac{54}{\pi}\sin\theta.
\]
Therefore \(\sin(\angle ABC)=\dfrac{\pi}{9}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Identify the circumference and height
